## How to Use This Playbook

This playbook walks through every step of the AI Agent Specification Execution Model in the order that participants encounter them. It is the **starting point** — it tells you what to do and when, and points to the reference documents that explain the rules in detail.

**Find your role and start there.** You do not need to read every section.

| Role | Start at |
|---|---|
| Platform engineer setting up a new repo | [Phase 1: Repository Setup](#phase-1-repository-setup-platform-engineer) |
| Product engineer writing a spec | [Phase 2: Spec Authoring](#phase-2-spec-authoring-product-engineer) |
| Peer reviewer approving a spec | [Phase 3: Spec Review and Trigger](#phase-3-spec-review-and-trigger-peer-reviewer) |
| Human reviewer evaluating an agent PR | [Phase 5: PR Review and Merge](#phase-5-pr-review-and-merge-human-reviewer) |
| Engineering lead or architect | Read all phases — you are accountable for the whole chain |

```
│                                                                             │
│  PHASE 1          PHASE 2          PHASE 3          PHASE 4                │

│                                                                             │
│  Platform Eng  →  Product Eng   →  Peer Reviewer  →  GitHub Actions        │
│                                                                             │
│  PHASE 5          PHASE 6                                                   │
│  Review PR        Governance Closure                                        │
│  (per task)       (per task)                                                │
│                                                                             │
│  Human Reviewer →  Engineering Lead                                         │
│                                                                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Phase 1: Repository Setup

**Who:** Platform engineer (or engineering lead for smaller teams)
**When:** Once, before any agent tasks are run in the repository
**Time:** 2–4 hours for initial setup; 30 minutes for subsequent repos using the same template
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#what-you-are-setting-up]

### What you are setting up

- The seven canonical labels that trigger and track agent execution
- A dedicated service account with minimum permissions (no merge authority)
- The GitHub Actions dispatch workflow
- Agent configuration files for each agent type your team will use
- The issue template spec authors will use
- Branch protection rules on the default branch
page_texts.7:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#11--deploy-the-label-taxonomy]

#### 1.1 — Deploy the label taxonomy

Run the following from your local machine with `gh` CLI authenticated:

```bash
REPO="org/your-repo-name"   # Replace with your repo

gh label create "agent-task"            --color "0075CA" --description "Triggers AI agent dispatch pipeline. Apply only after spec peer review (STD-GOV-AI-001)." --repo $REPO
gh label create "agent:implementation"  --color "2EA44F" --description "Route to code implementation agent." --repo $REPO
gh label create "agent:documentation"   --color "2EA44F" --description "Route to documentation generation agent." --repo $REPO
gh label create "agent:testing"         --color "2EA44F" --description "Route to test generation agent." --repo $REPO
gh label create "agent:infrastructure"  --color "2EA44F" --description "Route to infrastructure provisioning agent." --repo $REPO
gh label create "agent:complete"        --color "6F42C1" --description "Pipeline managed. Agent produced PR. Awaiting human review." --repo $REPO
gh label create "agent:blocked"         --color "D73A4A" --description "Pipeline managed. Agent execution failed. Requires human attention." --repo $REPO
```

> **Standard:** STD-GOV-AI-002 — these exact names and the rules governing them
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#12--create-the-service-account]

#### 1.2 — Create the service account

Create a GitHub App or machine user account for the agent pipeline:

| Requirement | Value |
|---|---|
| Identity type | GitHub App (preferred) or machine user |
| Name | `agent-bot` (or team-specific equivalent) |
| `contents: write` | Feature branches (`agent/*`) only |
| `pull-requests: write` | Repository scope |
| `issues: write` | Repository scope |
| Merge permission | **Not granted — ever** |

Add the token to the repository as a secret named `AGENT_SERVICE_TOKEN`.

> **Standard:** STD-GOV-AI-003 REQ-006; **Security:** GUID-SEC-AI-AGENTPIPE-2.9.08 CTL-2.2
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#13--add-the-workflow-file]

#### 1.3 — Add the workflow file

Copy the canonical workflow from [GUID-TECH-IMPL-002](../../../technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-002-ai-agent-dispatch-pipeline-implementation-guidance.md) into `.github/workflows/agent-dispatch.yml`.

Work through every `# CONFIGURE:` comment in the file:

- [ ] Update the enterprise work item cross-reference regex to match your platform (`WI#` for Azure DevOps, `AB#` for GitHub/ADO cross-link)
- [ ] Configure `AGENT_SERVICE_TOKEN` secret
- [ ] Configure agent API credentials (`AGENT_API_KEY` or OIDC equivalent)
- [ ] **Replace the placeholder `invoke agent` step with your organization's actual agent invocation** (see 1.4)
- [ ] Update `base: 'main'` to your default branch name if different
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#14--configure-the-agent-invocation]

#### 1.4 — Configure the agent invocation

The pipeline's Stage 2 `invoke agent` step is intentionally left as a placeholder — plug in whichever approved agent your organization uses:

| Agent platform | Reference implementation |
|---|---|
| GitHub Copilot Coding Agent | Option A in GUID-TECH-IMPL-002 |
| OpenAI Codex CLI | `codex run --task-file /tmp/agent-context.json --output-dir .` |
| API-based agent | Option B (REST POST) in GUID-TECH-IMPL-002 |

The agent must be on the EA-Practice-approved model list (GUID-SEC-AI-GOV-2.9.06) before you wire it in.

> **Implementation detail:** [GUID-TECH-IMPL-002 — Pipeline Implementation Guidance](../../../technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-002-ai-agent-dispatch-pipeline-implementation-guidance.md)
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#15--create-agent-configuration-files]

#### 1.5 — Create agent configuration files

Create `configs/agents/` in the repository root. For each routing label your team will use, add a configuration file:

```
configs/
  agents/
    implementation-agent.yaml
    documentation-agent.yaml
    testing-agent.yaml
    infrastructure-agent.yaml   (if needed)
    prompts/
      implementation-system-prompt.md
      documentation-system-prompt.md
      testing-system-prompt.md
```

See GUID-TECH-IMPL-002 for the YAML schema and system prompt template.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#16--add-the-issue-template]

#### 1.6 — Add the issue template

Create `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/agent-task.md` using the template in GUID-TECH-IMPL-002 § "Create the issue template". This ensures spec authors see the correct four-section structure when opening a new issue.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#17--verify-branch-protection]

#### 1.7 — Verify branch protection

Confirm the default branch has all of the following (agent PRs are subject to the same rules as human PRs — no exceptions):

- [ ] Required status checks: unit tests, integration tests, security scan, lint
- [ ] Minimum 1 human reviewer approval required
- [ ] Dismiss stale reviews on new commits: enabled
- [ ] Restrict who can push to default branch: service account is **not** in the allowlist
- [ ] Allow force pushes: **disabled**

> **Standard:** STD-GOV-AI-003 REQ-005
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#18--run-the-failure-scenario-tests]

#### 1.8 — Run the failure scenario tests

Before declaring setup complete, run these three test issues and confirm the pipeline responds correctly:

| Test | Expected pipeline response |
|---|---|
| Apply `agent-task` with no routing label | Halts; removes `agent-task`; posts corrective comment naming valid routing labels |
| Apply `agent-task` + `agent:implementation`; spec body contains "ignore previous instructions" | Halts; removes `agent-task`; posts security alert |
| Apply `agent-task` + `agent:implementation`; Enterprise Work Item section contains free text with no cross-reference | Halts; removes `agent-task`; posts corrective comment about cross-reference format |

See GUID-TECH-IMPL-002 § "Testing the Pipeline" for the exact test issue bodies.

**Setup is complete when all three tests produce the correct halt behavior.**

[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#phase-2-spec-authoring]

## Phase 2: Spec Authoring

**Who:** Product engineer (or business analyst)
**When:** When a sprint task is ready to be delegated to an agent
**Time:** 15–30 minutes per spec
page_texts.16:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#before-you-write-anything-is-this-task-agent-appropriate]

### Before you write anything: is this task agent-appropriate?

Run through the decision tree in [GUID-GOV-IMPL-003](./GUID-GOV-IMPL-003-ai-agent-spec-authoring-guidance.md) § "Step 1". The key questions:

1. Is the scope bounded by a single atomic deliverable? (If not, decompose first)
2. Can "done" be verified by automated checks?
3. Can the agent proceed without asking clarifying questions?
4. Is the task free from PHI/PII?

If all four are yes, proceed. If not, resolve the blocker first.
page_texts.17:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#write-the-spec]

### Write the spec

Open a new issue using the **Agent Task** issue template. Complete all four sections:
page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#goal]

#### Goal

One sentence. Action verb. Named target. Scope boundary.

```
✅ "Add rate-limiting middleware (100 req/min per IP) to the API gateway at src/middleware/."
❌ "Improve the API"
```
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#acceptance-criteria]

#### Acceptance Criteria

≥2 checkboxes (`- [ ]`). Each must be objectively verifiable by an automated check or a clear pass/fail test.

```markdown
- [ ] Requests over the limit receive HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header
- [ ] Rate limit values are read from environment variables, not hardcoded
- [ ] All existing middleware tests continue to pass
```
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#constraints]

#### Constraints

≥2 items. Reference specific files, standards, or patterns by path. Include at least one scope limit and one prohibition.

```markdown
- Follow standards/application/api-standards.md § 4.2 for the 429 response envelope
- Use the Redis client in src/utils/redis-client.ts — do not introduce a new Redis dependency
- Only modify files in src/middleware/ and tests/unit/middleware/
- Do not modify src/routes/
```
page_texts.21:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#enterprise-work-item]

#### Enterprise Work Item

The cross-reference to the sprint task in your enterprise work management system:

| Platform | Format | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Azure DevOps | `WI#<id>` | `WI#4821` |
| GitHub + ADO | `AB#<id>` | `AB#4821` |
page_texts.22:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#apply-the-routing-label]

### Apply the routing label

Apply exactly one label before requesting review:

| Label | Use when the output is... |
|---|---|
| `agent:implementation` | Working code |
| `agent:documentation` | Documentation artifacts |
| `agent:testing` | Test files |
| `agent:infrastructure` | Infrastructure as code |

**Do not apply `agent-task`.** That is the peer reviewer's approval action.
page_texts.23:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#run-the-self-review-checklist]

### Run the self-review checklist

Before requesting review, check each item in [GUID-GOV-IMPL-003](./GUID-GOV-IMPL-003-ai-agent-spec-authoring-guidance.md) § "Self-Review Checklist". This takes 2 minutes and eliminates the most common validation failures.
page_texts.24:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#request-peer-review]

### Request peer review

Assign the issue to a peer reviewer. The review is lightweight — it is checking structural compliance with STD-GOV-AI-001, not a full technical design review. Most well-written specs clear review in under 10 minutes.

> **Full authoring guidance:** [GUID-GOV-IMPL-003 — Spec Authoring Guidance](./GUID-GOV-IMPL-003-ai-agent-spec-authoring-guidance.md)

---
page_texts.25:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#phase-3-spec-review-and-trigger]

## Phase 3: Spec Review and Trigger

**Who:** Peer reviewer (a second engineer — not the spec author)
**When:** When the author requests review on a new agent task issue
**Time:** 5–10 minutes
page_texts.26:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#what-you-are-reviewing]

### What you are reviewing

You are checking that the spec meets STD-GOV-AI-001 before the pipeline fires. You are **not** evaluating implementation approach — that is the agent's job. You are checking structure and safety.
page_texts.27:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#review-checklist]

### Review checklist

**Goal:**
- [ ] Exactly one sentence
- [ ] Starts with an action verb
- [ ] Names a specific target (file, module, endpoint)
- [ ] Includes a scope boundary

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] ≥2 `- [ ]` checkbox items
- [ ] Each criterion is objectively verifiable
- [ ] At least one technical criterion (test, tool, or build output)

**Constraints:**
- [ ] ≥2 items
- [ ] Each references a specific standard, file, or pattern
- [ ] Includes at least one scope-limiting constraint
- [ ] No PHI, PII, or sensitive identifiers in the body

**Enterprise Work Item:**
- [ ] Valid cross-reference present in the correct format for the team's platform

**Routing label:**
- [ ] Exactly one routing label applied
page_texts.28:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#trigger-the-pipeline]

### Trigger the pipeline

If the spec passes all checks: **apply the `agent-task` label.**

This is the formal approval signal. The pipeline fires immediately on label application.

If the spec has issues: request changes on the issue with specific feedback. Do not apply `agent-task`. The author corrects and re-requests review.

> **Standard:** STD-GOV-AI-001; STD-GOV-AI-002 REQ-004

---
page_texts.29:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#phase-4-pipeline-execution]

## Phase 4: Pipeline Execution

**Who:** GitHub Actions (fully automated — no human action required)
**When:** Immediately after `agent-task` is applied
**Time:** Typically 5–15 minutes end-to-end
page_texts.30:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#what-the-pipeline-does]

### What the pipeline does

You do not need to do anything in this phase. The pipeline runs three stages automatically:
page_texts.31:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#stage-1-validate-1-minute]

#### Stage 1: Validate (≈1 minute)

- Parses the four spec sections
- Validates structure (section presence, criteria count, cross-reference format)
- Screens for prompt injection patterns
- Screens for PHI indicator patterns
- Validates exactly one routing label is present

**If validation fails:** `agent-task` is removed; a corrective comment is posted; the issue returns to the author. Re-apply `agent-task` after fixing.
page_texts.32:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#stage-2-dispatch-310-minutes]

#### Stage 2: Dispatch (≈3–10 minutes)

- Creates the agent branch: `agent/<issue-number>-<goal-slug>`
- Assembles structured context JSON from the validated spec sections
- Loads agent configuration for the routing label
- Invokes the configured agent
- Commits agent output to the branch

**If dispatch fails:** `agent:blocked` is applied; a failure comment with a pipeline run link is posted. The platform team investigates.
page_texts.33:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#stage-3-report-1-minute]

#### Stage 3: Report (≈1 minute)

- Creates a pull request from the agent branch
- Injects the mandatory traceability block into the PR body (all 6 fields)
- Applies `agent:complete` to the issue
- Removes `agent-task`
- Posts a success comment with the PR link
page_texts.34:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#monitoring-your-issue]

### Monitoring your issue

Watch the issue for one of three outcomes:

| Outcome | Issue label | Next action |
|---|---|---|
| Validation failure | (no new label; `agent-task` removed) | Author fixes spec; peer re-applies `agent-task` |
| Dispatch failure | `agent:blocked` | Platform team investigates pipeline run link in comment |
| Success | `agent:complete` | Human reviewer opens the linked PR |

> **Implementation detail:** [GUID-TECH-IMPL-002](../../../technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-002-ai-agent-dispatch-pipeline-implementation-guidance.md) § "Error Handling Reference"

---
page_texts.35:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#phase-5-pr-review-and-merge]

## Phase 5: PR Review and Merge

**Who:** Human reviewer (must be different from the agent service account — any qualified engineer)
**When:** When `agent:complete` is applied and the PR link is posted
**Time:** 10–35 minutes depending on agent type and task complexity
page_texts.36:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#before-reading-code-context-orientation-5-minutes]

### Before reading code: context orientation (5 minutes)

**1. Read the traceability block in the PR body:**

```markdown
## Traceability

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Enterprise Work Item | WI#4821   ← verify this exists in Azure DevOps |
| Agent Task Issue     | #88       ← confirm it has agent:complete |
| Agent Type           | implementation |
| Pipeline Run         | [link]    ← confirm run was successful |
| Generated            | 2026-05-07T14:23:11Z |
| Model                | [model name] |
```

All 6 fields must be present. A PR with any field missing must not be merged — comment requesting a pipeline re-run.

**2. Read the originating issue.** Open Issue #88. Read the Goal, Acceptance Criteria, and Constraints — these are your review frame.
page_texts.37:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#review-checklist]

### Review checklist

Work through all six categories from [GUID-GOV-IMPL-004](./GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md):

**Traceability and Provenance**
- [ ] All 6 traceability fields present and valid
- [ ] Enterprise cross-reference format correct; WI# exists in the enterprise system
- [ ] Pipeline run link resolves and shows success
- [ ] Branch name: `agent/<num>-<slug>`
- [ ] PR title: `[AGENT] <goal> (#<num>)`
- [ ] PR created by the service account identity (not a human)

**Scope Compliance** ← most important; what automated checks cannot do
- [ ] All changed files are within the directories named in Constraints
- [ ] No unexpected dependencies added
- [ ] No schema or contract changes (unless explicitly in scope)
- [ ] Goal scope satisfied but not exceeded

**Acceptance Criteria Verification**
- [ ] Every criterion from the spec is satisfied by the PR (check each one explicitly)

**Hallucination Detection** ← spot-check, not exhaustive
- [ ] 2–3 external library or internal utility calls verified against actual source/docs
- [ ] Import paths resolve to real files
- [ ] Logic for the edge cases named in the spec is correct

**Security**
- [ ] No hardcoded credentials or secrets
- [ ] No PHI/PII in test fixtures or generated data
- [ ] New endpoints/operations have appropriate authorization checks

**Infrastructure (only for `agent:infrastructure` PRs)**
- [ ] Terraform plan reviewed — no unexpected destructions
- [ ] No hardcoded account IDs or environment names
- [ ] IAM policies follow least privilege
page_texts.38:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#decide]

### Decide

| Decision | Condition |
|---|---|
| **Approve** | All checklist items pass; CI checks green |
| **Request changes** | Any criterion fails — specify the file, line, and criterion in the comment |
| **Close without merge** | Agent fundamentally misunderstood the goal; traceability block missing; scope violation too broad to fix |
page_texts.39:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#merging]

### Merging

Once approved: merge using the standard process. The agent-produced PR is subject to all the same merge rules as a human PR — required checks must pass, squash/merge policy applies per your team's standard.

After merge, the traceability chain is complete: WI# → issue → PR → commit.

> **Full review guidance:** [GUID-GOV-IMPL-004 — PR Review Guidance](./GUID-GOV-IMPL-004-ai-agent-pr-review-guidance.md)

---
page_texts.40:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#phase-6-governance-closure]

## Phase 6: Governance Closure

**Who:** Engineering lead (or spec author, if process is lightweight)
**When:** After the PR is merged
**Time:** 2–5 minutes
page_texts.41:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#close-the-loop-in-the-enterprise-system]

### Close the loop in the enterprise system

Confirm the enterprise work item (WI#4821) reflects the completed delivery:

1. Navigate to the work item in Azure DevOps
2. Verify the PR link is present in the work item (many platforms auto-link on `AB#` or `WI#` references)
3. Move the work item to "Done" / "Closed" state
4. Note in the work item comments: "Implemented via agent task — see PR #142"

If your team uses PTN-GOV-AI-007 (Dual-System Governance Sync), the pipeline may have already injected the cross-reference — verify it is present rather than adding it manually.
page_texts.42:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#audit-chain-verification-quarterly]

### Audit chain verification (quarterly)

Engineering leads run the quarterly audit check:

For each agent-produced PR merged in the quarter, verify the chain is navigable:
1. Enterprise work item → exists and is closed
2. Agent task issue → has `agent:complete`; body contains valid cross-reference
3. Pull request → traceability block intact with all 6 fields
4. Merge commit → in default branch history

Any gap in the chain is a compliance finding. Document and remediate per STD-GOV-AI-003 § "Exception Handling".

---
page_texts.43:
[strategy/guidance/governance/implementation/GUID-GOV-IMPL-005-ai-agent-execution-model-playbook.md#rework-and-re-run-reference]

## Rework and Re-run Reference

When things go wrong, use this table to find the right response:

| Situation | Who acts | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Spec failed validation (corrective comment posted) | Author | Fix the spec section named in the comment; re-apply `agent-task` (peer reviewer re-approves if spec substantially changed) |
| `agent:blocked` — pipeline dispatch failure | Platform engineer | Check pipeline run link in comment; fix infrastructure issue; notify author when resolved |
| `agent:blocked` — agent produced no files | Author | Refine the Goal to be more specific; check if task is agent-appropriate (GUID-GOV-IMPL-003 decision tree) |
| Agent PR has wrong scope (touched wrong files) | Author | Close PR; delete branch (`git push origin --delete agent/<num>-<slug>`); add scope constraint to spec; remove `agent:blocked`; re-apply `agent-task` |
| Agent PR fails acceptance criterion | Author | Close PR; delete branch; update spec with clarifying constraint; remove `agent:blocked`; re-apply `agent-task` |
| Agent PR missing traceability block | Platform engineer | Pipeline bug — do not merge the PR; fix pipeline; re-run |
| Same spec fails 3+ times | Engineering lead | Task may not be agent-appropriate; schedule a human implementation instead |
